# mlr3hf <img src="man/figures/block.png" align="right" width = "120" />


Package website: [release](writing/soon) | [dev](writing/soon)

Integration of [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co) datasets with the
[`mlr3`](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com/) ecosystem.

<!-- badges: start -->

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/anjaninandan001/mlr3hf/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/anjaninandan001/mlr3hf/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

## What is `mlr3hf`?

[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/) provides a large collection of datasets
for machine learning and data science. `mlr3hf` connects these datasets with
the [`mlr3`](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com/) ecosystem.

Datasets can be downloaded from Hugging Face and converted into `mlr3` data backends and tasks.

`mlr3hf` supports both Parquet datasets generated by Hugging Face and the
original dataset files stored in a repository.

As a brief demo, we download the Iris dataset from Hugging Face, convert it
into an `mlr3::Task`, and perform a simple resampling experiment.

```{r}
hf_data <- hfdt(
  repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris",
  config = "default",
  target = "Species",
  task_type = "classif"
)

task <- as_task(hf_data)

rr <- resample(
  task,
  lrn("classif.rpart"),
  rsmp("holdout")
)

rr$aggregate()
```

The same dataset can also be converted directly into an `mlr3::Task` using
`tsk()`:

```{r}
task <- tsk(
  "hf",
  repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris",
  config = "default",
  target = "Species",
  task_type = "classif"
)

task
```

## Working with Hugging Face datasets

`mlr3hf` provides two complementary entry points.

`hfdt()` creates an `HFData` object that provides access to the dataset and
its metadata. The object can subsequently be converted into an `mlr3`
`DataBackend` or `Task`.

```{r}
hf_data <- hfdt(
  repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris",
  config = "default",
  target = "Species",
  task_type = "classif",
  primary_key = "Id"
)

# Inspect the dataset
hf_data$data[1:5, ]

# Inspect metadata
hf_data$nrow
hf_data$ncol
hf_data$colnames
hf_data$feature_names
hf_data$splits
```

`tsk()` is a convenience function that creates an `mlr3::Task` directly,
without explicitly creating an `HFData` object first.

### Loading the original dataset files

When the original files stored in a Hugging Face repository should be used
instead of the generated Parquet dataset, specify `file_name`.

```{r}
hf_data <- hfdt(
  repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris",
  file_name = "Iris.csv",
  target = "Species",
  task_type = "classif",
  primary_key = "Id"
)

hf_data$data[1:5, ]
```

Depending on the arguments supplied, `mlr3hf` selects the appropriate loading
strategy:

* `repo_id`, `config`, `target`, and `task_type` load the dataset from the Hugging Face
  Parquet representation.
* `repo_id`, `file_name`, `target`, and `task_type` load the original dataset file from
  the Hugging Face repository.
* `primary_key` can be used to specify a column that uniquely identifies each row in the dataset.

## Feature Overview

* Hugging Face datasets can be converted directly into `mlr3` `Task` objects.
* Datasets can also be accessed as `HFData` objects and converted into
  `mlr3` `DataBackend` objects.
* Both Hugging Face-generated **Parquet** datasets and original
  **canonical dataset files** are supported.
* Predefined `train`, `test`, and `validation` splits can be used in
  `mlr3` resampling workflows.
* Datasets can be searched and retrieved using `list_datasets()`.
* Private and gated Hugging Face datasets can be accessed using authentication
  tokens.
* Downloaded datasets are cached locally to avoid repeated downloads.

## Predefined Dataset Splits

Many Hugging Face datasets provide predefined `train`, `test`, and
`validation` splits.

These splits are available through the `$splits` field of an `HFData` object
and can be used to construct custom `mlr3` resampling strategies.

```{r}
library("mlr3learners")

hf_data <- hfdt(
  repo_id = "a4n9i/scikit_iris",
  config = "default",
  target = "Species",
  task_type = "classif"
)

task <- as_task(hf_data)

train_row_id <- hf_data$splits$train
test_row_id <- hf_data$splits$test

resampling <- rsmp("custom")

resampling$instantiate(
  task,
  train_sets = list(train_row_id),
  test_sets = list(test_row_id)
)

rr <- resample(
  task,
  lrn("classif.rpart"),
  resampling
)

rr$aggregate()
```

## Listing Datasets

Datasets available on Hugging Face can be searched using `list_datasets()`.

For example, the following searches for five datasets related to
machine learning:

```{r}
list_hf_data <- list_datasets(
  num_of_dataset = 5,
  search = "machine learning"
)

list_hf_data
```

Datasets can also be filtered by author and the number of datasets to retrieve.

## Authentication

Authentication is required when accessing private or gated datasets.

`mlr3hf` looks for an authentication token in the following order:

1. `options(mlr3hf.hf_token = "...")`
2. `HF_TOKEN`
3. `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN`

An access token can be obtained from the Hugging Face account settings.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(mlr3hf.hf_token = "your_api_token")

Sys.setenv(HF_TOKEN = "your_api_token")

Sys.setenv(HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN = "your_api_token")
```

## Caching

Downloaded datasets are cached locally to avoid repeated downloads.

By default, the cache directory is:

```text
~/.cache/huggingface/
```

A different cache directory can be specified with:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(
  mlr3hf.cache_dir = "path/to/cache/directory"
)
```

## Documentation

The [package website](writing/soon) contains the complete
documentation and examples for `mlr3hf`.

For more information about data backends and the `mlr3` ecosystem, see the
corresponding [chapter](https://mlr3book.mlr-org.com/chapters/chapter10/advanced_technical_aspects_of_mlr3.html#sec-backends)
in the `mlr3` book.

The [Hugging Face documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs) is also a useful
resource for learning more about datasets and the Hugging Face Hub.

## Bugs, Questions, Feedback

`mlr3hf` is a free and open source software project that encourages
participation and feedback.

If you encounter a bug, have a question, or have a suggestion, please open an
[issue](writing/soon) on GitHub.

In case of problems or bugs, it is often helpful to provide a
**minimum working example** that reproduces the behaviour.
